The ONE\n    # release index is unmodified and still lists every released session, so\n    # restrict to the eids named there -- otherwise a session that is not on disk\n    # would be fetched over the network. The full dataset has no such file, and every\n    # session the index lists is on disk.\n    # Compare in string space: one.search returns UUID objects while the csv column\n    # is str, so a plain set intersection is empty whatever the contents. keep must\n    # stay UUID-valued for the `eid in keep` test below.\n    if subset_csv is not None:\n        subset_eids = set(pd.read_csv(subset_csv).eid.astype(str))\n        keep = {eid for eid in keep if str(eid) in subset_eids}\n        if not keep:\n            raise SystemExit(f'No sessions matched {subset_csv}; refusing to continue.')\n\n    eids, info = one.search(query_type='local', details=True)\n    selected = {}\n    for eid, session in zip(eids, info):\n        if eid in keep:\n            selected.setdefault(session['subject'], []).append(str(eid))\n    return {subject: selected[subject] for subject in sorted(selected)}\n\n\ndef camera_view(eid):\n    \"\"\"The side camera this session has whisker motion energy for, left preferred.\"\"\"\n    for view in ('left', 'right'):\n        if len(one.list_datasets(eid, filename=f'{view}Camera.ROIMotionEnergy.npy',\n                                 query_type='local')):\n            return view\n    raise ValueError(f'no whisker motion energy for {eid}')\n\n\n# --- trials ---\n\ndef trial_variables(trials):\n    \"\"\"Choice, block prior and trial number in block, one row per trial.\"\"\"\n    # probabilityLeft is constant within a block, so a change of value starts a new block\n    block = (trials.probabilityLeft != trials.probabilityLeft.shift()).cumsum()\n\n    return pd.DataFrame({'choice': trials.choice.map(CHOICE),\n                         'prior': trials.probabilityLeft.map(PRIOR),\n                         'trial_in_block': trials.groupby(block).cumcount()})\n\n\ndef covered(times, stim_on):\n    \"\"\"Trials whose window is spanned by this stream, allowing the one bin gap the reference allows.\"\"\"\n    start, stop = stim_on + T_START, stim_on + T_STOP\n    begin = np.searchsorted(times, start, side='right')      # first sample inside the window\n    end = np.searchsorted(times, stop, side='left') - 1       # last sample inside the window\n\n    # a trial with no sample at all, or a gap at either edge, has no usable trace\n    inside = begin <= end\n    first = np.where(inside, times[np.clip(begin, 0, times.size - 1)], np.inf)\n    last = np.where(inside, times[np.clip(end, 0, times.size - 1)], -np.inf)\n    return inside & (np.abs(start - first) <= BIN) & (np.abs(stop - last) <= BIN)\n\n\ndef usable_trials(trials, wheel_times, camera_times):\n    \"\"\"Trials the paper would keep, that also have a full wheel and camera window.\"\"\"\n    stim_on = trials.stimOn_times.to_numpy()\n    reaction = trials.firstMovement_times.to_numpy() - stim_on\n\n    keep = (reaction >= MIN_RT) & (reaction <= MAX_RT)          # NaN compares false, so those go too\n    keep &= trials.choice.isin(CHOICE).to_numpy()               # drops the no response trials\n    keep &= trials.probabilityLeft.isin(PRIOR).to_numpy()\n\n    return keep & covered(wheel_times, stim_on) & covered(camera_times, stim_on)\n\n\n# --- behavior ---\n\ndef window_slice(times, stim_on):\n    \"\"\"Index range of each trial window, so a stream is sliced rather than rescanned per trial.\"\"\"\n    window_start = stim_on + T_START\n    window_stop = stim_on + T_STOP\n\n    # the samples are in time order, so each window is one contiguous range of them\n    begin = np.searchsorted(times, window_start)\n    end = np.searchsorted(times, window_stop)\n\n    return begin, end\n\n\ndef trial_traces(times, values, stim_on):\n    \"\"\"A continuous trace resampled onto the same time grid for every trial.\"\"\"\n    begin, end = window_slice(times, stim_on)\n\n    traces = []\n    for trial, onset in enumerate(stim_on):\n        # one sample either side of the window, so the first and last bin centre are\n        # interpolated rather than clamped to the nearest sample inside it\n        first = max(begin[trial] - 1, 0)\n        last = end[trial] + 1\n\n        traces.append(np.interp(onset + TIME, times[first:last], values[first:last]))\n\n    return np.array(traces)\n\n\ndef discretize(trace):\n    \"\"\"Equal sized classes, split at percentiles of this session's own trace.\"\"\"\n    return np.digitize(trace, np.percentile(trace, SPLIT))\n\n\n# --- neural ---\n\ndef load_neural(eid):\n    \"\"\"Spike times and good clusters of a session, merged over its probes.\"\"\"\n    times, units, regions = [], [], []\n    for pid, name in zip(*one.eid2pid(eid)):\n        loader = SpikeSortingLoader(pid=pid, one=one, eid=eid, pname=name)\n\n        # skip the md5 check, which rereads every spike file and draws its own progress bar\n        spikes, clusters, channels = loader.load_spike_sorting(check_hash=False)\n\n        # a session can hold an insertion whose spike sorting was never released\n        if not clusters:\n            continue\n\n        clusters = loader.merge_clusters(spikes, clusters, channels)   # attaches metrics and histology\n\n        # `void` is the atlas label for a channel the histology placed outside the brain,\n        # so a unit there is not in a brain region at all\n        in_brain = brain_regions.acronym2acronym(\n            clusters['acronym'], mapping='Beryl') != 'void'\n\n        # spikes.clusters holds the row of the cluster table, so a per cluster flag\n        # can be indexed by it directly to say whether each spike survives\n        is_good = (clusters['label'] >= QC_LABEL) & in_brain\n        keep = is_good[spikes['clusters']]\n\n        # renumber the surviving clusters, continuing the count from the previous probe\n        new_index = np.cumsum(is_good) - 1\n        units.append(new_index[spikes['clusters'][keep]] + len(regions))\n        times.append(spikes['times'][keep])\n\n        # Beryl is the coarser atlas the reference code uses, e.g. DG-sg and DG-mo both become DG\n        regions.extend(brain_regions.acronym2acronym(clusters['acronym'][is_good], mapping='Beryl'))\n\n    times, units = np.concatenate(times), np.concatenate(units)\n\n    # sort the merged probes by spike time, as the reference does, so trials can be sliced\n    order = np.argsort(times, kind='stable')\n    return times[order], units[order], np.array(regions)\n\n\ndef spike_counts(times, units, n_units, stim_on):\n    \"\"\"Spike count per unit and bin, for every trial.\"\"\"\n    counts = np.empty((stim_on.size, n_units, N_BINS))\n    begin, end = window_slice(times, stim_on)\n\n    for trial, onset in enumerate(stim_on):\n        spike_time = times[begin[trial]:end[trial]] - onset      # time from stimulus onset\n        spike_unit = units[begin[trial]:end[trial]]\n\n        bin_index = np.floor((spike_time - T_START) / BIN).astype(np.int64)\n        \n        # a spike sitting on the window edge can round out of range once the onset is subtracted\n        bin_index = np.clip(bin_index, 0, N_BINS - 1)\n\n        # one flat index per spike lets a single bincount fill the whole unit by bin grid\n        flat_index = spike_unit * N_BINS + bin_index\n        counts[trial] = np.bincount(flat_index, minlength=n_units * N_BINS).reshape(n_units, N_BINS)\n\n    return counts\n\n\n# --- session ---\n\ndef process_session(eid, subject):\n    \"\"\"One session as lists of per trial neural, input and output arrays.\"\"\"\n    loader = SessionLoader(one=one, eid=eid)\n    loader.load_trials()\n    loader.load_wheel()\n    view = camera_view(eid)\n    loader.load_motion_energy(views=[view])\n\n    trials, wheel = loader.trials, loader.wheel\n    motion_energy = loader.motion_energy[f'{view}Camera']\n\n    variables = trial_variables(trials)                 # before filtering, so the block count is real\n    keep = usable_trials(trials, wheel.times.to_numpy(), motion_energy.times.to_numpy())\n    variables = variables[keep]\n    stim_on = trials.stimOn_times.to_numpy()[keep]\n\n    # no trial survived the mask, so there is nothing to load or bin\n    if stim_on.size == 0:\n        return {'session_id': str(eid), 'subject': subject, 'camera': view,\n                'neural': [], 'input': [], 'output': [],\n                'n_trials': 0, 'n_units': 0, 'regions': np.array([])}\n\n    speed = trial_traces(wheel.times, np.abs(wheel.velocity), stim_on)\n    whisker = trial_traces(motion_energy.times, motion_energy.iloc[:, 1], stim_on)\n\n    spike_times, spike_units, regions = load_neural(eid)\n    rate = spike_counts(spike_times, spike_units, regions.size, stim_on) / BIN\n\n    # the split is over the whole session, so both traces are discretized once, not per trial\n    speed_class = discretize(speed)\n    whisker_class = discretize(whisker)\n\n    neural = [trial.astype(np.float32) for trial in rate]\n    inputs, outputs = [], []\n    for trial in range(stim_on.size):\n        row = variables.iloc[trial]\n        inputs.append(np.stack([TIME, np.full(N_BINS, row.trial_in_block)]).astype(np.float32))\n        outputs.append(np.stack([np.full(N_BINS, row.choice), np.full(N_BINS, row.prior),\n                                 speed_class[trial], whisker_class[trial]]).astype(np.int8))\n\n    return {'session_id': str(eid), 'subject': subject, 'camera': view,\n OUTPUT_NAMES,\n        'output_values': OUTPUT_VALUES,\n\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nConvert the IBL brain-wide map (BWM) public release into the decoder-ready pickle format.\n\nUsage:\n    python -u /app/convert_data.py <outpicklefile> [--full | --sample] [--show-processing]\n\nThe conversion follows the reference pipeline of\n  Zhang et al., 'Exploiting correlations across trials and behavioral sessions to\n  improve neural decoding'  (code in /app/code/code_zhang2025)\nand the curation rules of\n  IBL et al., 'A brain-wide map of neural activity during complex behaviour'.\n\nTrials are aligned to stimulus onset, window (-0.5, +1.5) s, 20 ms bins -> T = 100.\n\nSee /app/CONVERSION_NOTES.md for the full rationale of every decision.\n\"\"\"\nimport /app/code/code_zhang2025/src/0_data_caching.py `params`\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\nALIGN_TIME = 'stimOn_times'\nTIME_WINDOW = (-0.5, 1.5)      # seconds relative to ALIGN_TIME\nBINSIZE = 0.02                 # seconds\nNBINS = int(np.ceil((TIME_WINDOW[1] - TIME_WINDOW[0]) / BINSIZE))   # 100\n\n# trial mask parameters -- reference 'firstMovement_times', 'feedbackType']\n\n# neuron curation -- data paper 'well-isolated neurons' + grey matter\nQC_LABEL = 1.0\nNON_GREY = ('root', 'void')\n\nBWM_RELEASE_CSV = '/app/code/code_zhang2025/data/bwm_release.csv'\n\nINPUT_NAMES = ['time_from_stim_on', 'trial_number_in_block']\nOUTPUT_NAMES = ['choice', 'prior_prob_left', 'wheel_speed', 'whisker_motion_energy']\nOUTPUT_VALUES = [\n    ['left', 'right'],\n    ['p_left_0.2', 'p_left_0.5', 'p_left_0.8'],\n    ['low', 'medium', 'high'],\n    ['low', 'medium', 'high'],\n]\nTRIAL_IN_BLOCK_SCALE = 100.0   # keeps the input O(1); see CONVERSION_NOTES Step 5\n\n\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Helpers\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\ndef get_one():\n    \"\"\"ONE instance that works offline against the staged cache.\n\n    NOTE: ONE() with no arguments reads ~/.one/.caches, which points CACHE_DIR at\n    /app/data/one_cache and lets dataset queries be answered from the cached Alyx REST\n    responses in .rest/.  Building ONE with an explicit tables_dir instead uses the\n    frozen release tables, which do NOT list the revisioned datasets that are actually on\n    disk (e.g. alf/#2025-03-03#/_ibl_trials.table.pqt) and silently returns a nearly empty\n    trials table.\n    \"\"\"\n    from one.api import ONE\n    return ONE()\n\n\ndef build_trials_mask(trials):\n    \"\"\"Reproduce reference ibl_data_utils.load_trials_and_mask(max_trial_len=10.).\n\n    Returns a boolean numpy array, True for trials to KEEP.\n    \"\"\"\n    query = f'(firstMovement_times - stimOn_times < {MIN_RT})'\n    query += f' | (firstMovement_times - stimOn_times > {MAX_RT})'\n    query += f' | (feedback_times - goCue_times > {MAX_TRIAL_LEN})'\n    for event in NAN_EXCLUDE:\n        query += f' | {event}.isnull()'\n    query += ' | (choice == 0)'\n    return np.asarray(~trials.eval(query), dtype=bool).copy()\n\n\ndef trial_number_in_block(prob_left):\n    \"\"\"0-based index of each trial within its block of constant probabilityLeft.\"\"\"\n    n = len(prob_left)\n    if n == 0:\n        return np.zeros(0, dtype=np.int64)\n    is_new = np.empty(n, dtype=bool)\n    is_new[0] = True\n    # NaN != NaN, so a NaN run would be split; treat NaNs as their own value.\n    prev, cur = prob_left[:-1], prob_left[1:]\n    is_new[1:] = ~((prev == cur) | (np.isnan(prev) & np.isnan(cur)))\n    block_start = np.maximum.accumulate(np.where(is_new, np.arange(n), 0))\n    return np.arange(n) - block_start\n\n\ndef bin_spikes_trials(spike_times, spike_clusters, n_clusters, t_beg):\n    \"\"\"Spike counts per (trial, cluster, bin).\n\n    Equivalent to the reference bincount2D(times, clusters, xbin=BINSIZE,\n    xlim=[t_beg, t_end]) truncated to NBINS bins, but computed for all trials at once.\n\n    Bin i of trial k covers [t_beg[k] + i*BINSIZE, t_beg[k] + (i+1)*BINSIZE).\n\n    Args:\n        spike_times:    (n_spikes,) sorted spike times, seconds\n        spike_clusters: (n_spikes,) cluster index in [0, n_clusters)\n        n_clusters:     number of clusters\n        t_beg:          (n_trials,) window start of each trial, seconds\n\n    Returns:\n        (n_trials, n_clusters, NBINS) float32 array of counts\n    \"\"\"\n    n_trials = len(t_beg)\n    out = np.zeros((n_trials, n_clusters, NBINS), dtype=np.float32)\n    if n_trials == 0 or len(spike_times) == 0:\n        return out\n\n    t_end = t_beg + NBINS * BINSIZE\n    # Trials are not necessarily time-ordered; searchsorted handles each independently.\n    i0 = np.searchsorted(spike_times, t_beg, side='left')\n    i1 = np.searchsorted(spike_times, t_end, side='left')\n\n    flat = out.reshape(n_trials, n_clusters * NBINS)\n    for k in range(n_trials):\n        a, b = i0[k], i1[k]\n        if b <= a:\n            continue\n        # bin index within the trial\n        bi = ((spike_times[a:b] - t_beg[k]) / BINSIZE).astype(np.int64)\n        np.clip(bi, 0, NBINS - 1, out=bi)\n        ci = spike_clusters[a:b]\n        np.add.at(flat[k], ci * NBINS + bi, 1.0)\n    return out\n\n\ndef interp_behavior(times, values, t_beg):\n    \"\"\"Linear interpolation of a continuous behaviour onto the bin RIGHT EDGES.\n\n    Matches reference get_behavior_per_interval, which evaluates at\n    np.linspace(interval_beg + binsize, interval_end, n_bins).\n\n    Returns (vals, ok) where vals is (n_trials, NBINS) and ok is (n_trials,) bool:\n    a trial is not ok if the trace does not cover its window (the reference\n    'target data starts too late' / 'ends too early' checks) or if any interpolated\n    value is NaN.\n    \"\"\"\n    n_trials = len(t_beg)\n    grid = BINSIZE * np.arange(1, NBINS + 1)                     # (NBINS,)\n    xi = t_beg[:, None] + grid[None, :]                          # (n_trials, NBINS)\n    ok = np.isfinite(t_beg)\n    if len(times) < 2:\n        return np.zeros((n_trials, NBINS), dtype=np.float32), np.zeros(n_trials, bool)\n\n    # coverage: the reference allows the trace to start/end within one binsize of the\n    # interval bounds.\n    t_end = t_beg + NBINS * BINSIZE\n    ok &= (t_beg >= times[0] - BINSIZE) & (t_end <= times[-1] + BINSIZE)\n\n    safe = np.where(np.isfinite(xi), xi, times[0])\n    vals = np.interp(safe, times, values).astype(np.float32)\n    ok &= np.isfinite(vals).all(axis=1)\n    return vals, ok\n\n\ndef tertile_bins(values, mask):\n    \"\"\"Discretise into 3 per-session classes at the 33.3 / 66.7 percentiles.\n\n    Thresholds are computed over every time bin of every KEPT trial of the session, so\n    the three classes are (near) equally populated within a session.\n    \"\"\"\n    pool = values[mask].ravel()\n    pool = pool[np.isfinite(pool)]\n    if pool.size == 0:\n        return np.zeros(values.shape, dtype=np.int64), (np.nan, np.nan)\n    lo, hi = np.percentile(pool, [100.0 / 3.0, 200.0 / 3.0])\n    if not (hi > lo):\n        # degenerate (e.g. a constant trace) -- fall back to unique-value splits\n        uq = np.unique(pool)\n        if uq.size >= 3:\n            lo, hi = uq[len(uq) // 3], uq[2 * len(uq) // 3]\n        elif uq.size == 2:\n            lo = hi = uq[0]\n        else:\n            lo = hi = uq[0]\n    cls = (values > lo).astype(np.int64) + (values > hi).astype(np.int64)\n    return cls, (float(lo), float(hi))\n\n\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Per-session conversion\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\ndef load_session(eid, probes, show_processing=False):\n    \"\"\"Load, curate, align and bin one session.\n\n    Args:\n        eid:     session UUID (str)\n        probes:  DataFrame rows of bwm_release.csv for this eid (pid, probe_name)\n\n    Returns a dict with the per-session arrays, or a dict with 'skip' set.\n    \"\"\"\n    from brainbox.io.one import SessionLoader, SpikeSortingLoader\n    from iblatlas.regions import BrainRegions\n\n    timings = {}\n    t_start = time.time()\n    one = get_one()\n    br = BrainRegions()\n\n    # ---------------- trials ------------------------------------------------------\n    t0 = time.time()\n    sl = SessionLoader(one=one, eid=eid)\n    sl.load_trials()\n    trials = sl.trials\n    if len(trials) == 0:\n        return {'eid': eid, 'skip': 'no trials'}\n    trial_mask = build_trials_mask(trials)\n    timings['trials'] = time.time() - t0\n\n    align = trials[ALIGN_TIME].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)\n    t_beg = align + TIME_WINDOW[0]\n    trial_mask &= np.isfinite(t_beg)\n\n    # ---------------- spikes ------------------------------------------------------\n    t0 = time.time()\n    spk_times, spk_clusters, acronyms, labels = [], [], [], []\n    offset = 0\n    for pid, pname in probes:\n        ssl = SpikeSortingLoader(pid=pid, one=one, eid=eid, pname=pname)\n        spikes, clusters, channels = ssl.load_spike_sorting()\n        if spikes is None or len(spikes) == 0 or 'times' not in spikes:\n            continue\n        cdf = SpikeSortingLoader.merge_clusters(spikes, clusters, channels).to_df()\n        # merge_probes: shift this probe's cluster ids so they are unique in the session\n        spk_times.append(np.asarray(spikes['times'], dtype=np.float64))\n        spk_clusters.append(np.asarray(spikes['clusters'], dtype=np.int64) + offset)\n        acronyms.append(cdf['acronym'].to_numpy().astype(str))\n        labels.append(cdf['label'].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64))\n        offset += len(cdf)\n    if offset == 0:\n        return {'eid': eid, 'skip': 'no spike sorting'}\n\n    spk_times = np.concatenate(spk_times)\n    spk_clusters = np.concatenate(spk_clusters)\n    acronyms = np.concatenate(acronyms)\n    labels = np.concatenate(labels)\n    n_units_all = len(acronyms)\n\n    # drop spikes with NaN times (can happen at the edges of a recording)\n    finite = np.isfinite(spk_times)\n    spk_times, spk_clusters = spk_times[finite], spk_clusters[finite]\n    order = np.argsort(spk_times, kind='stable')\n    spk_times, spk_clusters = spk_times[order], spk_clusters[order]\n    timings['spikes'] = time.time() - t0\n\n    # ---------------- neuron curation --------------------------------------------\n    beryl = np.asarray(br.acronym2acronym(acronyms, mapping='Beryl')).astype(str)\n    n_good = int((labels >= QC_LABEL).sum())\n    keep_unit = (labels >= QC_LABEL) & ~np.isin(beryl, NON_GREY)\n    if keep_unit.sum() == 0:\n        return {'eid': eid, 'skip': 'no well-isolated grey-matter units',\n                'n_units_all': n_units_all, 'n_good': n_good}\n    unit_idx = np.flatnonzero(keep_unit)\n    remap = np.full(offset, -1, dtype=np.int64)\n    remap[unit_idx] = np.arange(len(unit_idx))\n    new_clu = remap[spk_clusters]\n    sel = new_clu >= 0\n    spk_times_k, spk_clusters_k = spk_times[sel], new_clu[sel]\n    unit_regions = beryl[unit_idx]\n    n_neurons = len(unit_idx)\n\n    # ---------------- behaviour ---------------------------------------------------\n    t0 = time.time()\n    try:\n        sl.load_wheel()\n        wheel_t = sl.wheel['times'].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)\n        wheel_v = np.abs(sl.wheel['velocity'].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64))\n    except Exception:\n        return {'eid': eid, 'skip': 'no wheel'}\n\n    whisker_t = whisker_v = None\n    whisker_view = None\n    for view, key in (('left', 'leftCamera'), ('right', 'rightCamera')):\n        try:\n            sl.load_motion_energy(views=[view])\n            me = sl.motion_energy[key]\n            wt = me['times'].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)\n            wv = me['whiskerMotionEnergy'].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)\n            good = np.isfinite(wt) & np.isfinite(wv)\n            if good.sum() > 1:\n                whisker_t, whisker_v, whisker_view = wt[good], wv[good], view\n                break\n        except Exception:\n            continue\n    if whisker_t is None:\n        return {'eid': eid, 'skip': 'no whisker motion energy'}\n    timings['behavior'] = time.time() - t0\n\n    gw = np.isfinite(wheel_t) & np.isfinite(wheel_v)\n    wheel_t, wheel_v = wheel_t[gw], wheel_v[gw]\n\n    # Spike-sorting coverage.  The reference applies a coverage test to the behavioural\n    # traces (get_behavior_per_interval rejects an interval whose trace starts too late\n    # or ends too early) but not to the spikes, so a trial lying in a recording drop-out\n    # or past the end of the spike-sorted data silently becomes an all-zero matrix.\n    # Two real cases in this release: session 8c2f7f4d has three trials that start after\n    # its last spike, and session b182b754 has one trial inside a 2.1 s gap.  Apply the\n    # same rule to the neural stream.\n    spk_ok = np.zeros(len(t_beg), dtype=bool)\n    if len(spk_times_k) > 1:\n        t_end_all = t_beg + NBINS * BINSIZE\n        inside = np.isfinite(t_beg) & (t_beg >= spk_times_k[0] - BINSIZE) & \\\n                 (t_end_all <= spk_times_k[-1] + BINSIZE)\n        # a window must not fall inside a gap longer than the window itself\n        i0 = np.searchsorted(spk_times_k, np.where(inside, t_beg, spk_times_k[0]), 'left')\n        i1 = np.searchsorted(spk_times_k, np.where(inside, t_end_all, spk_times_k[0]), 'left')\n        spk_ok = inside & (i1 > i0)\n    trial_mask &= spk_ok\n\n    ws_vals, ws_ok = interp_behavior(wheel_t, wheel_v, t_beg)\n    wm_vals, wm_ok = interp_behavior(whisker_t, whisker_v, t_beg)\n    # reference align_spike_behavior: a trial survives only if it is good in the trials\n    # mask AND in every behaviour mask\n    keep_trial = trial_mask & ws_ok & wm_ok\n    if keep_trial.sum() < 2:\n        return {'eid': eid, 'skip': f'only {int(keep_trial.sum())} usable trials'}\n\n    # ---------------- discretise continuous outputs -------------------------------\n    ws_cls, ws_thr = tertile_bins(ws_vals, keep_trial)\n    wm_cls, wm_thr = tertile_bins(wm_vals, keep_trial)\n\n    # ---------------- per-trial variables -----------------------------------------\n    choice = trials['choice'].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)\n    # choice == +1 is a LEFT report, choice == -1 a RIGHT report (verified against\n    # contrastLeft/contrastRight and feedbackType).  Required coding: left = 0, right = 1.\n    choice_cls = (choice < 0).astype(np.int64)\n\n    p_left = trials['probabilityLeft'].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)\n    prior_cls = np.full(len(p_left), -1, dtype=np.int64)\n    prior_cls[np.isclose(p_left, 0.2)] = 0\n    prior_cls[np.isclose(p_left, 0.5)] = 1\n    prior_cls[np.isclose(p_left, 0.8)] = 2\n    keep_trial = keep_trial & (prior_cls >= 0)\n    if keep_trial.sum() < 2:\n        return {'eid': eid, 'skip': 'no trials with a valid probabilityLeft'}\n\n    tib = trial_number_in_block(p_left).astype(np.float32) / TRIAL_IN_BLOCK_SCALE\n\n    # ---------------- bin spikes (kept trials only) --------------------------------\n    t0 = time.time()\n    kt = np.flatnonzero(keep_trial)\n    binned = bin_spikes_trials(spk_times_k, spk_clusters_k, n_neurons, t_beg[kt])\n    timings['binning'] = time.time() - t0\n\n    # ---------------- assemble -----------------------------------------------------\n    time_axis = (TIME_WINDOW[0] + BINSIZE * np.arange(1, NBINS + 1)).astype(np.float32)\n\n    neural, inputs, outputs = [], [], []\n    for j, k in enumerate(kt):\n        neural.append(binned[j])\n        inp = np.empty((2, NBINS), dtype=np.float32)\n        inp[0] = time_axis\n        inp[1] = tib[k]\n        inputs.append(inp)\n        out = np.empty((4, NBINS), dtype=np.int64)\n        out[0] = choice_cls[k]\n        out[1] = prior_cls[k]\n        out[2] = ws_cls[k]\n        out[3] = wm_cls[k]\n        outputs.append(out)\n\n    res = {\n        'eid': eid,\n        'skip': None,\n        'neural': neural,\n        'input': inputs,\n        'output': outputs,\n        'regions': unit_regions,\n        'n_units_all': n_units_all,\n        'n_good': n_good,\n        'n_neurons': n_neurons,\n        'n_trials_raw': int(len(trials)),\n        'n_trials_mask': int(trial_mask.sum()),\n        'n_trials_kept': int(len(kt)),\n        'kept_trial_idx': kt.astype(np.int32),\n        'whisker_view': whisker_view,\n        'wheel_thresholds': ws_thr,\n        'whisker_thresholds': wm_thr,\n        'timings': timings,\n        'total_time': time.time() - t_start,\n    }\n    if show_processing:\n        res['_plot'] = {\n            'trials': trials, 'trial_mask': trial_mask, 'keep_trial': keep_trial,\n            'kt': kt, 't_beg': t_beg, 'time_axis': time_axis,\n            'wheel_t': wheel_t, 'wheel_v': wheel_v,\n            'whisker_t': whisker_t, 'whisker_v': whisker_v,\n            'ws_vals': ws_vals, 'wm_vals': wm_vals,\n            'ws_cls': ws_cls, 'wm_cls': wm_cls,\n            'ws_thr': ws_thr, 'wm_thr': wm_thr,\n            'binned': binned, 'spk_times_k': spk_times_k, 'spk_clusters_k': spk_clusters_k,\n            'regions': unit_regions, 'p_left': p_left, 'tib': tib,\n            'choice_cls': choice_cls, 'prior_cls': prior_cls,\n        }\n    return res\n\n\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Dataset Conversion Notes\n\n## Overview\n- **Dataset**: IBL Brain-wide map (public ONE cache in /app/data)\n- **Date started**: (see file mtime)\n- **Goal**: Convert to decoder-compatible format\n\n## Step 0: Setup and Initialization\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\nEnvironment: python3.13, numpy 2.3.5, torch 2.6.0+cu124, ONE api, brainbox, iblatlas all import OK.\nHardware: 128 CPUs, 1006 GB RAM, 1x NVIDIA L4 (23 GB).\n**No network access** - ONE must be used in pure offline (`mode='local'`) mode.\n\nDirectory contents of /app:\n- `.manifest`, `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yaml`, `stage_cache.sh` (infra)\n- `CONVERSION_NOTES.md` (this file)\n- `code/` -> `code_zhang2025/` (methods-paper code), `ibllib/` (IBL library source)\n- `data/one_cache/` -> ONE cache. Release tables in `Brainwidemap/`, `2022_Q4_IBL_et_al_BWM/`,\n  `2025_Q3_IBL_et_al_BWM/`; session data symlinked per lab (12 lab dirs).\n- `datapaper.pdf`, `methodpaper.pdf`, `dataarchitecture.pdf`, `methods.txt`\n- `decoder.py`, `train_decoder.py` (provided decoder)\n- `ibl_docs/` (offline docs)\n\nONE instantiation that works offline:\n```python\none = ONE(cache_dir='/app/data/one_cache',\n          tables_dir='/app/data/one_cache/Brainwidemap', mode='local')\n```\n(the default `tables_dir` is the cache root, where there are no tables)\n\n---\n\n## Step 1: Reference Code Exploration\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\nTwo code bases are provided in `/app/code`:\n- `code_zhang2025/` -- code for the **methods paper** (Zhang et al., \"Exploiting correlations\n  across trials and behavioral sessions to improve neural decoding\"). This is the decoding\n  pipeline whose data preparation I must match.\n- `ibllib/` -- source of the IBL library (`brainbox`, `ibllib`), used by the above.\n\n### Key Functions Identified\n| Function | File | Stage | Purpose |\n|----------|------|-------|---------|\n| top-level script | `src/0_data_caching.py` | LOADING/PROCESSING | Whole preprocessing pipeline; sets `params` (alignment, window, bin size) and `beh_names` |\n| `prepare_data(one, eid, bwm_df, params)` | `src/utils/ibl_data_utils.py` | LOADING | Per session: `one.eid2pid` -> loop over probes -> `load_spiking_data` -> `merge_probes`; `load_trials_and_mask(max_trial_len=10.)`; `load_anytime_behaviors` |\n| `load_spiking_data(one, pid, qc=None)` | ibl_data_utils.py | LOADING | `SpikeSortingLoader(pid,...).load_spike_sorting()` + `SpikeSortingLoader.merge_clusters(...).to_df()`. **`qc=None` by default => returns ALL clusters**; if `qc=1` it keeps `clusters.label >= 1` |\n| `merge_probes(spikes_list, clusters_list)` | ibl_data_utils.py | PROCESSING | Concatenates probes of one session into a single population, re-indexing `spikes['clusters']`, re-sorting spikes by time |\n| `load_trials_and_mask(one, eid, min_rt=0.08, max_rt=2., nan_exclude='default', max_trial_len=10., exclude_nochoice=True)` | ibl_data_utils.py | CURATION | `SessionLoader.load_trials()` then builds a boolean trial mask |\n| `list_brain_regions` / `select_brain_regions` | ibl_data_utils.py | PROCESSING | `BrainRegions().acronym2acronym(acronyms, mapping='Beryl')`; with `single_region=False` selects the union of all regions (i.e. all clusters) |\n| `bin_spiking_data(reg_clu_ids, neural_df, trials_df, **params)` | ibl_data_utils.py | PROCESSING | intervals = `trials_df[align_time] + time_window`; bins with `iblutil.numerical.bincount2D(times, clusters, xbin=binsize, xlim=[t_beg,t_end])`, truncated to `n_bins = ceil(interval_len/binsize)`. Returns `(n_trials, n_bins, n_clusters)` |\n| `load_target_behavior(one, eid, target)` | ibl_data_utils.py | LOADING | `SessionLoader.load_wheel()` (`wheel-speed` = `abs(velocity)`); `SessionLoader.load_motion_energy(views=['left'/'right'])` -> `motion_energy['leftCamera']['whiskerMotionEnergy']` |\n| `get_behavior_per_interval(...)` | ibl_data_utils.py | PROCESSING | Slices the continuous trace to each interval, then `interp1d(kind='linear')` onto `np.linspace(beg+binsize, end, n_bins)` (i.e. **bin right edges**). Marks an interval bad if: no samples, NaNs (when `allow_nans=False`), NaN interval bounds, trace starts >1 binsize after the interval start, or ends >1 binsize before the interval end |\n| `bin_behaviors(one, eid, behaviors, trials_df, ...)` | ibl_data_utils.py | PROCESSING | Per-trial scalars straight from the trials table: `choice = trials.choice`, `block = trials.probabilityLeft`, `reward = (rewardVolume > 1)`, `contrast = -(nan_to_num(contrastLeft) + ... )`; plus the time-varying behaviors above |\n| `align_spike_behavior(binned_spikes, binned_behaviors, beh_names, trials_mask)` | ibl_data_utils.py | CURATION | Deletes trials that are bad in the trials mask **or** in any behavior mask, so neural and behavior have identical trials |\n| `standardize_spike_data` / `SingleSessionDataset` | `src/utils/data_loader_utils.py` | PROCESSING | Downstream modelling only: z-scores spikes per (time bin, neuron) and z-scores continuous behaviour per session; discrete behaviour is one-hot encoded |\n\n### Parameters used by the reference pipeline (`src/0_data_caching.py`)\n```python\nparams = {'interval_len': 2, 'binsize': 0.02, 'single_region': False,\n          'align_time': 'stimOn_times', 'time_window': (-.5, 1.5)}\nbeh_names = ['choice', 'reward', 'block', 'wheel-speed', 'whisker-motion-energy']\n```\n=> 2 s trials aligned to **stimulus onset**, 20 ms bins, **T = 100**. Note that\n`pupil-diameter` is commented out because \"Some sessions do not have pupil traces\".\n\n### Notes\n- `load_trials_and_mask` is called with `exclude_unbiased=False`, so the 90 unbiased\n  (pLeft = 0.5) trials at the start of a session are **kept**. This matters here because\n  `probabilityLeft` is one of our decoder outputs with three classes (0.2/0.5/0.8).\n- The freeze file `data/bwm_release.csv` (699 rows) is the authoritative list of\n  (pid, eid, probe_name, subject, lab) in the brain-wide map release.\n- `qc=None` in `load_spiking_data` means the reference decoding code used *all* Kilosort\n  clusters, consistent with the methods paper (\"we bin spike counts using all neurons\").\n  See Step 4 for how I reconcile this with the data paper's neuron inclusion criteria.\n\n---\n\n## Step 2: Dataset Exploration\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\n### Data Structure\nThe data live in a standard **ONE cache** at `/app/data/one_cache`:\n\n```\n/app/data/one_cache/\n  Brainwidemap/            datasets.pqt (76,563), sessions.pqt (480)   <- release tables\n  2022_Q4_IBL_et_al_BWM/   datasets.pqt (38,814), sessions.pqt (354)\n  2025_Q3_IBL_et_al_BWM/   datasets.pqt  (5,339), sessions.pqt (459)\n  .rest/                   6,483 cached Alyx REST responses\n  <lab>/Subjects/<subject>/<yyyy-mm-dd>/<nnn>/    <- session data (12 labs, 461 session dirs)\n      alf/  _ibl_trials.table.pqt (usually under revision dir `#2025-03-03#`),\n            _ibl_wheel.position.npy / .timestamps.npy,\n            leftCamera.ROIMotionEnergy.npy, rightCamera.ROIMotionEnergy.npy,\n            _ibl_leftCamera.times.npy, _ibl_{left,right}Camera.dlc.pqt, licks, passive...\n      alf/<probe>/pykilosort/  spikes.{times,clusters,amps,depths}.npy,\n            clusters.{channels,depths,metrics.pqt,uuids.csv,waveforms}.npy,\n            channels.{brainLocationIds_ccf_2017,mlapdv,localCoordinates,rawInd}.npy\n      raw_ephys_data/<probe>/  *.ap.meta (used for sampling frequency)\n```\n\n**Important access detail.** Many files on disk sit in *revision* folders\n(e.g. `alf/#2025-03-03#/_ibl_trials.table.pqt`, present for 454/461 sessions) that are\nnewer than any of the three staged release tables. Consequently\n`ONE(cache_dir=..., tables_dir=.../Brainwidemap, mode='local')` silently returns an almost\nempty trials table (only `goCueTrigger_times`). The staging script copies ONE's parameter\nfile and a `.rest` cache of Alyx REST responses, so the correct (and intended) call is\nsimply\n\n```python\none = ONE()          # reads ~/.one/.caches -> cache_dir=/app/data/one_cache, mode='remote'\n```\n\nwhich resolves dataset queries from the cached REST responses and therefore *does* find\nthe revisioned datasets. All loading below uses this instance. **This was the single most\nimportant discovery of Step 2** -- the alternative silently produces a broken dataset.\n\n### Available variables\n- **Trials** (`SessionLoader.load_trials()` -> 20 columns): `stimOn_times`,\n  `stimOnTrigger_times`, `stimOff_times`, `stimOffTrigger_times`, `goCue_times`,\n  `goCueTrigger_times`, `response_times`, `firstMovement_times`, `feedback_times`,\n  `feedbackType`, `choice`, `contrastLeft`, `contrastRight`, `probabilityLeft`,\n  `rewardVolume`, `quiescencePeriod`, `intervals_0/1`, `intervals_bpod_0/1`.\n  - `choice` in {-1, 0, +1}. Verified empirically on eid 6713a4a7...: on rewarded trials\n    with a left stimulus `choice == +1` always, and with a right stimulus `choice == -1`\n    always. So **choice = +1 means the mouse reported LEFT**, `choice = -1` reports RIGHT,\n    `choice = 0` is a no-go. (The sign is the wheel direction, not the stimulus side.)\n  - `probabilityLeft` in {0.2, 0.5, 0.8}; 0.5 only in the first 90 (unbiased) trials.\n- **Wheel** (`SessionLoader.load_wheel()`): `times`, `position`, `velocity`,\n  `acceleration`, resampled to a uniform 1000 Hz grid (median dt = 1/1024 s) with\n  Gaussian-smoothed velocity. ~4.7 M samples/session.\n- **Motion energy** (`SessionLoader.load_motion_energy(views=['left'])`):\n  `times`, `whiskerMotionEnergy` at the camera rate (left = 60 Hz, right = 150 Hz).\n- **Spike sorting** (`SpikeSortingLoader(pid).load_spike_sorting()` +\n  `merge_clusters`): `spikes.times/clusters`, and a cluster table with\n  `acronym`, `atlas_id`, `x/y/z`, `depths`, `firing_rate`, `amp_median`, `noise_cutoff`,\n  `slidingRP_viol`, `label`, `ks2_label`, `bitwise_fail`, `uuids`, ...\n  - `label` is the IBL single-unit QC score in {0, 1/3, 2/3, 1}: the fraction of the three\n    RIGOR single-unit criteria passed (median amplitude > 50 uV, noise cut-off < 20 uV,\n    refractory-period violation). `label == 1` == **well-isolated neuron**.\n\n### Dataset Size (measured from the data files, all 699 insertions scanned)\n| Statistic | Value |\n|-----------|-------|\n| Insertions (probes) | 699 |\n| Sessions (eids) | 459 |\n| Subjects (mice) | 139 |\n| Labs | 12 |\n| Units (total, all Kilosort clusters) | **621,733** |\n| Well-isolated units (`label >= 1`) | **75,708** |\n| ... of those, in Beryl grey matter (not `root`/`void`) | 65,301 |\n| Well-isolated grey-matter units / session | mean 142.3 (all 459 sessions have >= 1) |\n| Distinct Beryl regions with well-isolated grey-matter units | 265 |\n| Sessions with a left-camera whisker ME trace | 437 |\n| Sessions with a right-camera whisker ME trace | 433 |\n| Sessions with either | 445 |\n| Sessions with wheel and trials | 459 / 459 |\n| Trials / session (raw) | e.g. 565 for eid 6713a4a7...; typically 300-900 |\n\nThe 621,733 and 75,708 figures reproduce the data paper **exactly**, which validates\nboth the loading path and my interpretation of `clusters.label`.\n\nNo `DATALIMIT_SUBSET.csv` is present, so the **full 459-session release** is to be\nprocessed.\n\n---\n\n## Step 3: Reference Text Reading\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\n### Expected Statistics (from papers/methods)\n| Statistic | Value | Source Quote |\n|-----------|-------|--------------|\n| Sessions in release | 459 | \"a total of 459 sessions, 699 insertions and 621,733 neurons remained, constituting the publicly released dataset\" (data paper) |\n| Insertions | 699 | same |\n| Units (all) | 621,733 | same |\n| Well-isolated neurons | 75,708 | \"Out of the 621,733 units collected, 75,708 were considered well-isolated neurons\" |\n| Subjects (mice) | 139 (94 M, 45 F) | \"We trained 139 mice (94 male and 45 female)\" |\n| Sessions used in Fig. 1d | 454 | \"Data are for 139 mice and 454 sessions\" |\n| Sessions in methods paper | 433 | \"We apply our models to 433 IBL sessions, covering 270 brain regions\" |\n| Brain regions (methods paper) | 270 | same |\n| Trials / session (release criterion) | >= 250 | \"Sessions were included in the data release if the mice performed at least 250 trials\" |\n| Unbiased block | first 90 trials, pLeft = 0.5 | \"Each session started with 90 trials in which the probability ... was equal\" |\n| Biased block length | 20-100, truncated exponential, scale 60, empirical mean 51 | \"Blocks lasted for between 20 and 100 trials ... (empirical mean of 51 trials)\" |\n| Block probabilities | 20:80 or 80:20 | \"at a ratio of 20:80% (right block) or 80:20% (left block)\" |\n| Contrasts | 100, 25, 12.5, 6.25, 0 % in ratio 2:2:2:2:1 | \"Stimulus contrast was uniformly sampled from 5 possible values\" |\n| **Reaction times < 80 ms** | **22.8% of trials** | \"A total of 22.8% first wheel-movement times occurred under 80 ms\" |\n| Performance on 0% contrast | 58.7 +- 0.4% correct | Fig. 1d caption |\n| Neural time bin (choice, stimOn-aligned) | 20 ms (methods paper code) / 50 ms (methods paper text for choice+prior) | see below |\n| Trial length | 2 s -> T = 100 bins | \"Recordings are split into 2-s trials, each divided into 20-ms bins, producing T = 100 time steps\" |\n| Behaviour sampling rate | 60 Hz | \"wheel speed and whisker motion energy are ... sampled at 60 Hz\" |\n\n### Processing Details\n\n**Temporal alignment.** The methods paper: \"For choice, we align trials to the stimulus\nonset, considering neural activity from 0.5 s before to 1.5 s post-onset.\" The reference\ncode implements exactly this for *all* of its behaviours in one pass:\n`align_time='stimOn_times'`, `time_window=(-.5, 1.5)`, `interval_len=2`, `binsize=0.02`.\nThe decoder task here also specifies **\"Temporally align based on stimulus onset\"**, so\nthis is the alignment and window I use: **`off_start = -0.5 s`, `off_end = +1.5 s`,\n20 ms bins, T = 100**.\n\n**Bin-size discrepancy in the paper text.** The text says 50 ms bins for the\nchoice/prior decoders and 20 ms for the dynamic behaviours, but the abstract/model\nsection and the actual released code both use 20 ms with T = 100. Because a single\ndataset must serve all four outputs here (two per-trial, two time-varying), I follow the\ncode and the model description: **20 ms, T = 100**.\n\n**Temporal binning.**\n- Spikes: counts in `[stimOn - 0.5 + i*0.02, stimOn - 0.5 + (i+1)*0.02)` for i = 0..99,\n  exactly `bincount2D(..., xbin=0.02, xlim=[t_beg, t_end])` truncated to 100 bins.\n- Behaviour: linearly interpolated onto the **right edge** of each bin,\n  `np.linspace(beg + binsize, end, 100)`, exactly as `get_behavior_per_interval`.\n\n### Curation Steps\n\n**Session curation rules** (already applied to the release): >= 250 trials, >= 90% correct\non 100% contrast in both block types, >= 3 incorrect trials, hardware QC passed,\nresolved histology alignment, RIGOR whole-recording criteria.\n\n**Neuron curation rules** (data paper):\n> \"Neurons ... were excluded ... if they failed one of the three criteria ...: amplitude >\n> 50 uV; noise cut-off < 20 uV; and refractory period violation. Neurons that passed these\n> criteria were termed well-isolated neurons.\"\n\nThis is exactly `clusters.label == 1` (the label is the fraction of the three criteria\npassed). 358\t\n   359\t    tib = trial_number_in_block(p_left).astype(np.float32) / TRIAL_IN_BLOCK_SCALE\n   360\t\n   361\t    # ---------------- bin spikes (kept trials only) Uses `searchsorted`\n  to isolate each trial window and `np.add.at` on a flat view. Equivalent to the\n  reference `bincount2D(..., xbin=0.02, xlim=[t_beg, t_end])[:, :100]` but for all trials\n  at once and without the reference multiprocessing pool per trial.\n- `interp_behavior(...)` -- linear interpolation onto bin right edges\n  `t_beg + 0.02*(1..100)`, plus the reference coverage checks (trace must start no more\n  than one bin after, and end no less than one bin before, the window).\n- `tertile_bins(...)` -- per-session 33.3/66.7 percentile discretisation.\n- `load_session(eid, probes)` -- the whole per-session pipeline.\n- `make_processing_plot(res, outfile)` -- a 7x4 diagnostics figure (see Step 7).\n- `main()` -- `ProcessPoolExecutor` over sessions, assembly, statistics, pickling.\n\n### Code inefficiencies identified and removed\n- The reference bins spikes with a `multiprocessing.Pool` **per trial** and calls\n  `bincount2D` once per trial. Replaced with one `searchsorted` for all trials plus a\n  single `np.add.at` per trial -- about 2 orders of magnitude fewer Python-level calls.\n- The reference calls `get_behavior_per_interval` (another per-trial process pool) for\n  each behaviour. Replaced with a single vectorised `np.interp` over an\n  `(n_trials, 100)` grid.\n- Spike sorting is loaded once per probe, and the trials/wheel/motion-energy objects once\n  per session, via a single shared `SessionLoader`.\n- Parallelism is at the **session** level (`ProcessPoolExecutor`), which is the natural\n  grain and avoids the reference nested-pool overhead.\n- Only the kept trials are binned, so no work is done for trials that will be discarded.\n\n### Bug found and fixed during development\n- `(~trials.eval(query)).to_numpy()` returns a **read-only** array, so the subsequent\n  in-place `trial_mask &= ...` raised `ValueError: output array is read-only` and every\n  session was silently skipped. Fixed with an explicit\n  `np.asarray(..., dtype=bool).copy()`. This is exactly the kind of failure the\n  per-session try/except would otherwise have hidden, so the driver prints the skip\n  reason for every session.\n\n---\n\n## Step 7: Sample Conversion and
